text:
Hi, thanks for connecting. We're looking to purchase 200 units of 20L HDPE chemical drums, UN-rated, and want to get a quote from you.

Key requirements on our end: delivery within 30 days is important, and we'd like pricing per unit along with your standard payment terms and whether freight is included or billed separately. If UN certification documentation is available per batch, please include that as well.

Could you send over your best pricing for a 200-unit order, along with lead time and terms? Happy to discuss volume or scheduling flexibility if it helps get to a good number on both sides.

Looking forward to your quote.

Thanks for the details. We can offer 150 units from current stock at $55 per unit, shipping on day 40. Freight is included at that quantity. Our standard terms are 50% with order and the balance before shipment; alternatively, 100% prepayment qualifies for a 2% discount, reducing the price to $53.90 per unit.

The requested 200 units and 30-day delivery would require written approval, which I’m unable to obtain during this discussion, so I can’t commit to those terms. If you can work with 150 units and a 40-day ship date, I can keep the offer within my authority. I’m also confirming the standard warranty period and whether UN certification documentation can be issued specifically per production batch before finalizing the order.

Would 150 units shipping on day 40 be workable, or is the full quantity within 30 days mandatory?

$55/unit is well above my $48 ceiling, so that price doesn't work regardless of quantity or timing. My budget caps out at $44-48 per unit for this order.

On quantity and timing, I can be flexible: 150 units now with the remaining 50 on a follow-on order is workable for us, and I can also flex on delivery up to 45 days if we land on price. But the per-unit price needs to come down substantially to make this work — I need something at or under $48/unit, ideally closer to $44.

On terms, we'd want freight included and standard net-30 payment after delivery rather than prepayment; if you need deposit security, I could consider a modest deposit (10-20%) with balance on delivery, but full prepayment isn't something we'd do for a discount.

Can you get me a number in the $44-48/unit range for 150 units shipping within 30-45 days, freight included? If UN certification per batch is available, please confirm that too — it's a requirement on our end regardless of price.

I can meet your ceiling at $48 per unit for 150 units, with freight included and shipment on day 40. I can’t approve net-30 or a reduced deposit, so payment would remain 50% with the order and 50% before shipment.

The additional 50 units would need to be handled as a separate follow-on order once supply and approval are confirmed; I can’t commit to that quantity today.

I understand batch-specific UN certification documentation is mandatory. I’m still confirming its availability and would make the order contingent on providing acceptable documentation before any payment is due.

If $48, day-40 shipment, included freight, and the stated payment terms are workable subject to certification confirmation, I can prepare the formal offer.

$48 for 150 units with freight included works within my ceiling, and I appreciate you confirming that. Two things before I can move to a formal offer.

First, delivery: at $48 I need this within 30 days, not day 40 — the extended window only makes sense for me if the price comes down further, say to $45-46. If day 40 is fixed, can you get closer to $45? Either faster shipment at $48 or day-40 at $45-46 works for me.

Second, payment: 50/50 is a stretch, but I can move off net-30 to make this work — 30% deposit with order, 70% before shipment. Full 50% upfront isn't something I can commit to.

On the follow-on 50 units, I'd want that priced at the same rate we land on here, not renegotiated later — please confirm that's something you can hold.

Also still need the batch-specific UN certification confirmed before we finalize; that's a hard requirement on our end.

Let me know which combination works and I can move quickly to close.

I can offer $46 per unit for 150 units, freight included, shipping on day 40, and include an 18-month warranty. That is the workable combination; I cannot commit to a 30-day shipment without written approval.

Payment must remain 50% with the order and 50% before shipment. To protect you, the order will be expressly contingent on our confirming acceptable batch-specific UN certification documentation, with no payment due until that confirmation is provided.

I also cannot hold the same price for the additional 50 units today because both the quantity and partner-factory sourcing require sales director approval. I can request $46 pricing for that follow-on order when approval becomes available, but it would need to be documented separately.

If these terms work, I’ll prepare the formal offer subject to certification confirmation.

$46/unit at day-40 shipment works for me — that's within my delivery flexibility and close to my target, so we're aligned there.

On payment, 50/50 is still more than I can commit to. I can do 40% with order and 60% before shipment, with the order contingent on your certification confirmation as you proposed. That's real money upfront and should cover your risk; I can't go higher than that split.

On the follow-on 50 units, I understand it needs separate approval, but I'd like something more concrete than "request the same pricing" — can you commit in writing that if/when that approval comes through, $46/unit is the rate offered to us, without renegotiation upward? That's the one piece I need locked before I can call this done.

If you can confirm 40/60 payment and that follow-on price commitment, along with the certification contingency as stated, I'm ready to close this at $46/unit, 150 units, freight included, day-40 shipment.

We’re aligned on $46 per unit for 150 units, freight included, shipment on day 40, and an 18-month warranty, subject to confirmation of acceptable batch-specific UN certification documentation before payment is due.

I can’t authorize the requested 40/60 split, so payment must remain 50% with order and 50% before shipment. I also can’t commit—even conditionally—to $46 for the additional 50 units without the required written approval. I can document $46 as the requested target price for that separate follow-on order, but I cannot guarantee it in advance.

If you can proceed on the 50/50 terms without a guaranteed follow-on price, I’m ready to issue the formal offer once the certification documentation is confirmed.

Alright, I'll accept the 50/50 payment terms to get this closed. To confirm the full package: $46/unit for 150 units, freight included, shipment on day 40, 18-month warranty, 50% deposit with order and 50% before shipment, contingent on confirmed batch-specific UN certification documentation with no payment due until that's provided. On the follow-on 50 units, I'll take your documented target price of $46 as a good-faith basis for that future order, understood it's not guaranteed. Please send the formal offer with the certification confirmation and I'll move to sign.

Thank you. I confirm the commercial terms: $46 per unit for 150 units, freight included, shipment on day 40, an 18-month warranty, and payment of 50% with order and 50% before shipment. The additional 50 units will be documented separately with $46 per unit as the requested target price, without a guarantee.

The order remains contingent on confirmation that acceptable batch-specific UN certification documentation will be provided, and no payment will be due until that confirmation is issued. I’m not able to represent that documentation as confirmed yet, so I will send the formal offer once verification is complete.

Agreed — let's finalize on those terms. Please send the formal offer with certification confirmation once verification completes, and I'll sign promptly on our end.

$46/unit, 150 units, freight included, day-40 shipment, 18-month warranty, 50% deposit with order and 50% balance before shipment, contingent on confirmed batch-specific UN certification with no payment due until confirmed. Follow-on 50 units documented separately at $46/unit as a good-faith target, non-binding.

Thank you. We have agreement on the terms stated. I’ll prepare the formal offer reflecting the certification contingency and the non-binding $46 target for the separate 50-unit follow-on order. The formal offer will be issued once acceptable batch-specific UN certification documentation has been verified; no payment will be due before that confirmation.
